issue_context.title: Support Decorators Maintaining Signatures of Generic Functions
issue_context.body:
As a follow up to #27393 I think I made a mistake in just typing some of the return values to be `Callable`. The following script highlights that issue:

```python
from pandas.util._decorators import Appender

def func1(num: int) -> int:
    return num

@Appender("")
def func2(num: int) -> int:
    return num

reveal_type(func1)
reveal_type(func2)
```

If you run that from the project root you'll get something like the following:

```sh
$ mypy foo.py
foo.py:10: note: Revealed type is 'def (num: builtins.int) -> builtins.int'
foo.py:11: note: Revealed type is 'def (*Any, **Any) -> Any'
```

We probably want to maintain the types of the signature for `func2` so I think need to use TypeVar for generic support. 

More info on the mypy side in:

https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/3113
https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/1551

So I think need something like:

```python
T = TypeVar('T', bound=Callable[..., Any])
# then decorators can return
-> Callable[[T], T]
```
comments: Does ``reveal_type`` return the proper types if this change is made?
@simonjayhawkins you recently had a solution for this right? Interested in extending it too pandas.util._decorators?

@WillAyd I'm reopening this as #28128 did not close this issue. solved for `Appender` and `Substitution` only

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/commit/dd957415cb367056a6f58a776090c5efb581735e will fix `deprecate_kwarg` and probably similar for `rewrite_axis_style_signature`
Sounds good - thanks for taking a look

This should already be resolved here:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/6f2c60ea99fd17e40d3e67195eebacddc2e445cb/pandas/_typing.py#L101

review_comments: Is the bound required here? I thought only had to do with class inheritance so not sure if there's actually something for the Callable or if this is an undocumented feature
this is to declare a decorator that preserves the signature of the function it decorates, regardless of that signature. https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generics.html#declaring-decorators
Is this required because of inheritance? Not used in function body AFAICT so somewhat odd
yes. subclasses should have the same or additional arguments. not less.
I think OK just to do `Dict` instead of `Dict[Any, Any]`; same thing but more readable

it is the same thing but would fail --disallow-any-generics check.

although readability is important, i don't think the benefits of precise type checking can be understated.
